newsitem.title: UK: NORTH SEA CRUDE EASES ON IRAQ, SLACK U.S. DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: NORTH SEA CRUDE EASES ON IRAQ, SLACK U.S. DEMAND.

text.p: North Sea crudes weakened again in early talk on Thursday amid expectations that Iraq will start exporting oil as early as next Monday and traders saw little U.S. demand for Dated Brent.
"Iraq is pushing people to nominate as early as possible. The first shipments will probably be around August 11-15," said a trader.

Sept Brent shed 16 cents to trade at $19.04 a barrel by 1028 GMT and intermonth cash spreads also weakened a couple of cents from late Wednesday levels, with Sep/Oct and Oct/Nov both talking around -12 cents.
Traders said slack interest for Dated Brent in the U.S. Gulf, where sellers are having to compete with unsold August Nigerian barrels, was also depressing sentiment.
"Dated is going to have to lose another 10 cents today," said a trader.
The benchmark was pegged at around Sept Brent -5 cents in early talk, down from the last reported deal at +3 cents.

An Aug 21-23 Brent cargo, clocked to Wall Street trader Aron, was deferred and moving through the forward paper chains on Thursday. The second cargo due to turn wet was kept early by equity holder Shell.

The most visible impact of the imminent resumption of Iraqi exports was, as expected, in the Mediterranean sour market where a French refiner was reported to have sold Russian Urals at the equivalent of Dated Brent -90/-95 cents a barrel on Wednesday.
The previous reported deal was about 40 cents higher, traders said.
"That level is not too far away from the market at the moment," said a trader.
A European major was still trying to move a prompter cargo loading around Aug 12-14, he added.
